lead: A one-way slab bends mainly in the short direction. Take a 1 m wide strip along the short span and design it as a beam. This works when the long span ly is at least twice the short span lx. The strip carries the full factored load w in kN/m. Use Mu = wl²/8, Vu = wl/2, then find steel from Mu/bd²fck. Add distribution steel at right angles and check shear, deflection and cracking. This is the common floor slab in buildings.
prereq: You need Unit 1 (partial safety factors, stress block) and Unit 2 (singly reinforced flexure, Mu/bd²fck); see 4.2 for the two-way case.

sections.h3: Why the short span carries the load

blocks.text: A slab is a plate supported on edges. Under load it curves in both directions. The stiffness of a unit-width strip against bending varies as 1/l⁴, where l is the span of that strip. If the long span ly is twice the short span lx, the short strip is 2⁴ = 16 times stiffer. The short direction then carries about 16/17 ≈ 94% of the load. IS 456 treats a slab as one-way when ly/lx ≥ 2. Some syllabi call this simply a slab spanning one way.

The design takes a 1 m wide strip spanning the short direction. This strip is a beam of width b = 1000 mm and depth h equal to the slab thickness. The effective depth is d = h - clear cover - φ/2, where φ is the main bar diameter in mm. A load of w kN/m² on the slab becomes a line load of w kN/m on the strip. The unit is kN per metre of strip, not kN total.

A simply supported strip uses Mu = wl²/8 and Vu = wl/2. Continuous slabs use code coefficients that allow for pattern loading (see 4.3). A cantilever slab has hogging moment at its support. This chapter uses the simply supported case. If ly/lx < 2, the slab bends in both directions and must be designed as a two-way slab (see 4.2).

sections.h3: Design steps for a 1 m strip

items: Pick a trial thickness h. For a simply supported one-way slab, basic span/effective depth is 20 for mild steel. For Fe415 multiply by 0.8, giving about 16. Use a round value such as 100 mm, 110 mm or 120 mm.
Find the effective span l. Use clear span plus effective depth, or centre-to-centre of supports, whichever is less. For small bearings many designs take l equal to clear span.
Build the load per m²: self weight = 25h (h in m), floor finish, and live load. Total service load = DL + LL. Factored load w = 1.5(DL + LL).
Compute moment and shear per metre strip: Mu = wl²/8 and Vu = wl/2.
Compute d = h - clear cover - φ/2 with b = 1000 mm. Check Mu ≤ 0.138 fck b d² for Fe415.
Find steel area Ast from the flexure formula. Take the larger of Ast required and the minimum steel.
Minimum steel is 0.12% of b h for Fe415 (0.15% for mild steel).
Fix spacing: main bars ≤ min(3d, 300 mm); distribution bars ≤ min(5d, 450 mm). Distribution steel area ≥ 0.12% b h.

blocks.where: w is the factored load in kN/m on the 1 m strip; l is the effective span in m; Mu is in kN·m per metre width.

blocks.text: Mu = 0.87 fy Ast d (1 - fy Ast / (fck b d))
blocks.where: fy is steel strength in N/mm²; Ast is steel area in mm²; d is effective depth in mm; b = 1000 mm; fck is concrete strength in N/mm².

blocks.text: Shear check: τv = Vu/(b d). The design shear strength τc is read from IS 456 Table 19 using pt = 100 Ast/(b d). A slab has no shear reinforcement, so it must satisfy τv ≤ k·τc, where k is the depth factor from IS 456 clause 40.2.1.1 (about 1.30 for h ≤ 150 mm, falling to 1.00 for h ≥ 300 mm). Using k = 1 is always safe. If the check fails, increase the thickness h.

Deflection check: basic span/depth is 20 for simply supported, 26 for continuous, and 7 for cantilever. Multiply by the modification factor for tension steel. The modified ratio must be at least l/d. A 120 mm slab on a 3 m span has l/d ≈ 31.6; low steel gives a modification factor that can make it acceptable. Always check.

Crack control: keep main bar spacing ≤ 300 mm and distribution bar spacing ≤ 450 mm. Provide nominal cover of 20 mm for mild exposure (this may be taken as 15 mm when the main bar is 12 mm or smaller) and 30 mm for moderate exposure, as per IS 456 Table 16. Distribution steel runs at right angles to the main steel. It holds the main bars during casting, resists shrinkage and temperature stresses, and spreads local loads.

examples.question: A simply supported one-way slab has a clear span of 3.0 m between 230 mm walls; the effective span is 3.0 m. Live load 3.0 kN/m², floor finish 1.0 kN/m², thickness 120 mm, M25 concrete, Fe415 steel, clear cover 20 mm. Find the factored moment and the main and distribution steel.
steps: Thickness h = 120 mm = 0.12 m. Self weight = 0.12 × 25 = 3.0 kN/m². Floor finish = 1.0 kN/m². Live load = 3.0 kN/m². Total service load = 3.0 + 1.0 + 3.0 = 7.0 kN/m².
Factored load w = 1.5 × 7.0 = 10.5 kN/m². On a 1 m strip, w = 10.5 kN/m.

Effective span by the Section 2 rule: clear span + d = 3.0 + 0.095 = 3.095 m (d = 95 mm from step 4), and centre-to-centre of supports = 3.0 + 0.230 = 3.23 m. The lesser is 3.095 m. This example takes l = 3.0 m only as a conservative simplification, which slightly over-designs the slab. Then Mu = wl²/8 = 10.5 × 3.0² / 8 = 11.8125 kN·m per m, and Vu = wl/2 = 10.5 × 3.0 / 2 = 15.75 kN per m.
Effective depth: clear cover 20 mm, assume 10 mm bar. d = 120 - 20 - 10/2 = 95 mm. b = 1000 mm.
Limiting moment: Mu,lim = 0.138 fck b d² = 0.138 × 25 × 1000 × 95² = 31.14 × 10⁶ N·mm = 31.14 kN·m. Mu = 11.8125 < 31.14, so the section is under-reinforced.
Minimum steel = 0.12% of b h = 0.0012 × 1000 × 120 = 144.0 mm²/m. Required 368.2 > 144.0, so use 368.2 mm²/m.
Spacing of 10 mm bars: area of one bar = 78.54 mm². Spacing = 1000 × 78.54 / 368.2 = 213.3 mm. Use 200 mm c/c, which provides 392.7 mm²/m.

Distribution steel = 144.0 mm²/m. Use 8 mm bars, area 50.27 mm². Spacing = 1000 × 50.27 / 144.0 = 349 mm. Maximum allowed = min(5d, 450) = min(475, 450) = 450 mm. Use 250 mm c/c, which provides 201.1 mm²/m.
examples.answer: The factored load is 10.5 kN/m², Mu = 11.8125 kN·m per metre, Vu = 15.75 kN per metre, main steel 368.2 mm²/m (use 10 mm @ 200 mm c/c), distribution steel 144.0 mm²/m (use 8 mm @ 250 mm c/c).
examples.check:
w_dead = 0.12*25 + 1.0
w_live = 3.0
w_serv = w_dead + w_live
w_u = 1.5*w_serv
l = 3.0
Mu = w_u*l*l/8
Vu = w_u*l/2
b = 1000.0
h = 120.0
cover = 20.0
phi = 10.0
d = h - cover - phi/2
fck = 25.0
fy = 415.0
Au = Mu*1e6
term = 1 - 4.6*Au/(fck*b*d*d)
Ast = 0.5*fck/fy*(1 - term**0.5)*b*d
Ast_min = 0.0012*b*h
print(round(w_u, 1))
print(round(Mu, 4))
print(round(Vu, 2))
print(round(Ast, 1))
print(round(Ast_min, 1))

traps: Writing the total load in kN instead of kN/m. On a 1 m strip, a load of 10.5 kN/m² becomes 10.5 kN/m.
Using the full slab width (say 3 m) in Mu/bd². Take b = 1000 mm for a 1 m strip.
Forgetting distribution steel. It is at least 0.12% of b h for Fe415 and runs at right angles to the main steel.
Using the wrong cover when finding d. Take clear cover, not effective cover, and subtract half the bar diameter.

quiz.a: A slab with ly/lx ≥ 2, designed as a 1 m strip spanning the short direction only.

quiz.q: Why does the short span carry most of the load when ly/lx ≥ 2?
quiz.a: Stiffness varies as 1/l⁴. For ly = 2lx, the short strip is 16 times stiffer and carries about 16/17 of the load.

quiz.q: A one-way slab has factored load 12 kN/m² and effective span 2.5 m. Find Mu per metre width.
Why is distribution steel provided in a one-way slab?
quiz.a: It holds main bars during casting, resists shrinkage and temperature stresses, and spreads local loads. It is not the main bending steel.

quiz.q: What is the minimum steel in a 120 mm thick Fe415 slab, per metre width?
Find d for h = 140 mm, clear cover 20 mm, 12 mm bar.
Shear check fails for a one-way slab. What are two practical fixes?
quiz.a: Increase slab thickness to raise d and reduce τv; or increase concrete grade. Shear reinforcement is not usual in thin slabs.

quiz.q: Why is b taken as 1000 mm in slab design?
quiz.a: A 1 m strip is a convenient unit. The slab is uniform, so the design of 1 m represents the whole slab.

beyond: Not for the exam. Finite element analysis shows how load really spreads in a slab. Yield line theory gives the collapse load for unusual shapes (see 4.6). Flat slabs skip beams and carry load to columns (see 4.5). Search 'one-way slab design IS 456' and 'slab effective span' for more.
